utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Would the registrar please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you. And good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-95-5/18-R77.2, in the Contempt Case of Milan Tupajic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I have the appearances.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours. My name is Aleksandar Lazarevic. I'm counsel for Mr. Tupajic in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Lazarevic. Mr. Tupajic, could you confirm whether you following the proceedings in a language that you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am receiving the signal, but the sound is too low, and I cannot understand what is being said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Our usher will assist you in a minute. Mr. Tupajic, I hope that you are hearing me better now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's okay now. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tupajic. Today, prior to the commence of the trial, pursuant to Rule 73 bis (A) of the Tribunal's Rules of Procedure and Evidence, we are holding a pre-trial conference in order to discuss how the trial should be conducted. First, Mr. Lazarevic, turning to the schedule of this trial, I take it that you have seen our decision on the motion to postpone the trial issued -- which was issued on 17th January. The Chamber explained that, given the courtroom schedule of the Tribunal, and the Judges' commitments on other trials, the only time available, other than today, would be either Monday, 23rd of January, or Friday, 3rd of February. Given that Mr. Tupajic is in detention, which date would be preferable for you and your client?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And I have to say it's unfortunately the first time -- I didn't discuss this issue with Mr. Tupajic. I drew his attention to the fact that most of these documents that I referred in -- to -- to -- that I spoke with him about and that I received from Mr. Tupajic has not been translated. But given the fact that I requested, like, ten days of delay in the proceedings, I believe that February 3rd would be much more in favour of Mr. Tupajic. Because this time, if allotted, would be -- it's more than sufficient to prepare his evidence and all the documents, and my estimation is that it won't take more than one day of trial to complete this -- this trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If necessary, we can adjourn for you to have a word with your client.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I believe that Mr. Tupajic already showed me that it's okay for the February 3rd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Tupajic, can you confirm that the 3rd of February would suit you?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely. As far as I am concerned, I can stand trial on Monday. However, if the date in February suits the Trial Chamber, I'm not opposed to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So, Mr. Lazarevic, you prefer to have the trial on 3rd of February.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Then it is ordered that the trial of Mr. Tupajic for contempt of the Tribunal be held on Friday, 3rd of February, 2012. And having heard that, I take it that you can withdraw your motion.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And that's precisely what I'm going to do. I always follow Your Honours' advices.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Next, Mr. Lazarevic, then I would like to know whether the Defence will make an opening statement, pursuant to Rule 84.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are not going to make an opening statement. We will just start with the evidence of Mr. Tupajic. And, furthermore, we intend not to call any witnesses whatsoever. We will rely solely on Mr. Tupajic's evidence and the documents that will be tendered through Mr. Tupajic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lazarevic. Then by your submission I take it that the accused himself does not wish to make a statement pursuant to Rule 84 bis of the Rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then how long do you expect Mr. Tupajic's evidence to last?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: If everything goes well, I was trying to assess the way Mr. Tupajic speaks. He is a fast speaker, and I believe that it will take maybe two, up to three hours, not more than this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So I take it, including your submission, and closing argument of the accused, it will be sufficient as a one-day trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tupajic, do you have any issues you like to raise about the conditions of your detention here at -- at the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I must say now, and I did it already during the recess, that the attitude of the staff in the Detention Unit is very fair. I'm enjoying very good conditions there, which means that I don't have any objections or complaints about my stay in the Detention Unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tupajic. Mr. Lazarevic, I wonder if there are any other issues you like to raise at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, in order to -- to cover all the aspects of this case, I was advised by Mr. Tupajic - because that was one of the issues that I discussed with him in the Detention Unit while I was visiting him - he basically told me that he was not examined well by various specialists, and having -- bearing in mind, maybe we should move it into private session for a very brief moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Could the Chamber move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Other than the issue we discussed in private session, are there any matters, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Then hearing is now adjourned until 3rd of February.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 3rd day of February, 2012, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 9.16 a.m.,
